results.name: Lat Pull Down Wide Grip
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with both hands, wider than shoulder-width apart, and your arms fully extended above you.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your back straight.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward excessively.
Focus on engaging your back muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Lat Pull Down Wide Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Lawnmower Row
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one hand on your front thigh or a bench, holding a dumbbell in the other hand.
Hinge forward with a flat back and let the dumbbell hang below your shoulder.
Pull the weight up and back toward your hip, rotating your torso slightly as you would starting a lawnmower.
Lower the weight with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Lead with your elbow and keep it close to your body.
Keep the rotation small and controlled.
results.description: Lawnmower Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Obliques.

results.name: Lying Back Extension
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed behind your head, elbows out to the sides.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your upper torso off the floor, keeping your neck in a neutral position and your lower body relaxed on the floor.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your lower back muscles.
Slowly lower your upper torso back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you find it challenging to lift your upper torso, you can start with smaller movements and gradually increase the range of motion as you build strength.
results.description: Lying Back Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Plate Alternating Deadstop Row
instructions: Place two weight plates on the floor and hinge over them with a flat back, knees slightly bent.
Grip one plate and row it up toward your hip.
Lower it back to the floor and let it come to a full stop.
Row the other plate and keep alternating.
tips: Each rep starts from a dead stop, so don't bounce the plate.
Keep your torso still as you pull.
results.description: Plate Alternating Deadstop Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Plate Glute Bridge to Pullover
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a weight plate above your chest with both hands.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a glute bridge.
Holding the bridge, lower the plate behind your head with slightly bent arms until you feel a stretch in your lats.
Pull the plate back over your chest, then lower your hips and repeat.
tips: Keep your ribs down while the plate moves overhead.
Squeeze your glutes throughout the bridge.
results.description: Plate Glute Bridge to Pullover is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Chest, Triceps.

results.name: Plate Good Morning
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hold a weight plate against your chest.
With a slight bend in your knees, hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Lower your torso until it is close to parallel with the floor, or until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
tips: Keep your back flat; don't round it to go lower.
Push your hips back rather than bending your knees more.
results.description: Plate Good Morning is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Plate Pinch Grip Deadlift
instructions: Stand over two weight plates and pinch one in each hand by its rim, fingers on one face and thumb on the other.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees with a flat back.
Drive through your feet to stand up tall, holding the plates at your sides.
Lower them back down with control by hinging at your hips.
tips: The pinch grip limits the weight, so this is mainly a grip and posture drill.
Keep your shoulders back and chest up.
results.description: Plate Pinch Grip Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Quadriceps, Traps.

results.name: Plate Pinch Grip Row
instructions: Pinch a weight plate in one hand and hinge forward with a flat back, supporting yourself on a bench or your thigh with the other hand.
Let the plate hang below your shoulder.
Row the plate up toward your hip by driving your elbow back.
Lower it with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Keep the plate from swinging.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
results.description: Plate Pinch Grip Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Rear Shoulders.

results.name: Prone Bench Row Barbell Pronated Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a barbell with a pronate grip (palms facing down) and your hands placed shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches close to the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
results.description: Prone Bench Row Barbell Pronated Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Prone Bench Row Barbell Reverse Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing up) and your hands placed shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Pull the barbell towards your abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches close to the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Keep your elbows close to your body to maximize back muscle engagement.
results.description: Prone Bench Row Barbell Reverse Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.
